liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls the Other One smokin' within a hypnotic, trippy second set; The Other One space is included within the Other One track [5][23]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review): Brent's keyboard part on Dupree's has a carnival-like sound that the reviewer loves [30]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Reviewer describes a very enthusiastic Wharf Rat [28]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 other source): The Music Never Stopped into Deal ends in an immediate fade-out, so the full song is patched from source 9947 [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Down In the Bottom**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 10 archived performances [33]
- Earliest performances in the archive: NFA chant, NFA chant [33]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-04-12.fob.senn421.colyard.ford.93961.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 28 songs; 188 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1983-04-12.138560.Senn421.FOB.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 180 min [2]
- **gd1983-04-12.124253.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 177 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [3]
- **gd1983-04-12.163638.senn441.neumann.u87.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 177 min [5]
- **gd83-04-12.sbd.dodd.10075.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 3.68/5 by 31 [12]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is pretty decent for its era, with a few bumps early that improve as the show goes on; Nice soundboard, much clearer than a muddy board the reviewer got years earlier [21][25]
- **gd83-04-12.wise.sacks.9947.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [13]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds crisp and very loud, matching the show itself [28]
- **gd83-04-12.set2.pcm-sbd.miller.30808.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 101 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [18]. Said about its sound: Second-set sound is called easily five stars, among the best-sounding shows the reviewer has downloaded [32]

## Around the show

- Reviewer lived in Scranton, PA, about a 45-minute drive away, and went to the show without his friend John Ruby [22]
- Jerry wore red tees on this tour, and the Binghamton crowd felt like a private Avalon Ballroom dance party [24]
- Reviewer drove from Mt. Snow, VT, not knowing where Broome County was, and found a nice small venue [28]
- This was the last show the Grateful Dead ever played in Binghamton, NY [36]
- Reviewer sees 1983 as a turning point with very hot versions of standard songs, this show included [25]
- Reviewer thinks April 1983 shows may beat the September-October ones, with this second set a prime example [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-04-12.fob.senn421.colyard.ford.93961.flac16**: taped by Rick "Coyote" Colyard; transferred by Alex Ford; source: (FOB) 2 x Sennheiser 421 > Sony D5 > 2 x Maxell UDXL II C90 Location: 20th Row center. [1]. Also: Front-of-board Sennheiser 421 recording by Colyard and Ford, from master audience cassettes supplied by Muletaper; Tape flips and other patches come from source 9947 [1]
- **gd1983-04-12.138560.Senn421.FOB.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Rick Gastwirt;Charlie Miller;Joe Noel; source: flac16/48kHz ; Unknown Taper (FOB): Sennheiser 421 > cassette master* > dat; Charlie Miller [2]. Also: Main source is Jim Wise's Sennheiser front-of-board recording, shnid 9947; Patches come from Brian Schley's Nak front-of-board recording and Rick Colyard's Sennheiser front-of-board recording, mainly in Drums and the encore break [2]
- **gd1983-04-12.124253.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by dusborne; source: 3 Source Matrix by Dusborne: Soundboard (shnid:17264) Set 1SBD > Cassette master > Dats > CDR > SHN by drgseeds, Soundboard (shnid:30808) Set 2 Recording Info:… [3]. Also: This is a matrix mix, with the listing credited to dusborne [3]
- **gd1983-04-12.163638.senn441.neumann.u87.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441's (left + right) + (1) Neumann U87 (center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [5]
- **gd83-04-12.sbd.dodd.10075.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>PCM>DAT>CDR (Has Analog Gen) [12]. Also: Reviewer had a crystal-clear first-generation Nak audience tape of the show the day after it happened; Reviewer says this is not a PCM recording; it includes analog generations [23][26]
- **gd83-04-12.wise.sacks.9947.sbeok.shnf**: source: Jim Wise recording, FOB Sennheuser 421s>Sony D5>DAT>CDR [13]
- **gd83-04-12.set2.pcm-sbd.miller.30808.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: flac16 SBD -> PCM Master -> PCM Clone -> Sonic Solutions -> Dat [18]. Also: Charlie Miller released a 16-bit FLAC version of the second set from a PCM soundboard source [32]

claims.text: Soundboard is pretty decent for its era, with a few bumps early that improve as the show goes on
Reviewer lived in Scranton, PA, about a 45-minute drive away, and went to the show without his friend John Ruby
Reviewer had a crystal-clear first-generation Nak audience tape of the show the day after it happened
Reviewer calls the Other One smokin' within a hypnotic, trippy second set
Jerry wore red tees on this tour, and the Binghamton crowd felt like a private Avalon Ballroom dance party
Nice soundboard, much clearer than a muddy board the reviewer got years earlier
Reviewer sees 1983 as a turning point with very hot versions of standard songs, this show included
Reviewer says this is not a PCM recording; it includes analog generations
Audience recording sounds crisp and very loud, matching the show itself
Reviewer drove from Mt. Snow, VT, not knowing where Broome County was, and found a nice small venue
Reviewer describes a very enthusiastic Wharf Rat
Brent's keyboard part on Dupree's has a carnival-like sound that the reviewer loves
Charlie Miller released a 16-bit FLAC version of the second set from a PCM soundboard source
Second-set sound is called easily five stars, among the best-sounding shows the reviewer has downloaded
Reviewer thinks April 1983 shows may beat the September-October ones, with this second set a prime example
Front-of-board Sennheiser 421 recording by Colyard and Ford, from master audience cassettes supplied by Muletaper
Tape flips and other patches come from source 9947
The Music Never Stopped into Deal ends in an immediate fade-out, so the full song is patched from source 9947
Main source is Jim Wise's Sennheiser front-of-board recording, shnid 9947
Patches come from Brian Schley's Nak front-of-board recording and Rick Colyard's Sennheiser front-of-board recording, mainly in Drums and the encore break
This is a matrix mix, with the listing credited to dusborne
Set II comes from Rob Eaton's recording and transfer, coordinated by Charlie Miller
Colyard and Ford's Sennheiser 421 source supplies a 5:48 patch in Drums
The Other One space is included within the Other One track
This was the last show the Grateful Dead ever played in Binghamton, NY
